title: Elodie and the Songbook
premise: Cyrus Dunmore built her café and her careful, guarded life on the ruins of a love she abandoned at twenty-four: Elodie Marsh, the folk singer who chose a touring career over her. Ten years later, a snowstorm traps them together in the shuttered mountain inn where they first met, forcing old wounds and an unfinished songbook into the open. As Cyrus fights to save her failing café back home, she and Elodie rediscover what they were to each other—and who they've become—until Cyrus must choose between the anonymity that kept her safe and a love that demands to be seen. In the end, she signs the loan papers that keep her café alive but sells her stake in it, moving to join Elodie on tour as the duo's resident baker, finally singing backup in a life she no longer hides from.
about_author: Hazel Yarrow is the pen name of a former line cook who spent a decade writing love stories on the backs of order tickets before publishing her first novel. She lives in a coastal town where every café knows her order and none of them know her name.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. She opens her café before dawn, counts the bank notices taped inside the register, and performs cheerfulness for regulars while calculating exactly how many weeks of solvency remain. Emotional beat: weary denial—the cost of building a life that looks stable from the outside.

chapters.title: The Letter with a Mountain Postmark
chapters.summary: Cyrus receives an invitation to a winter festival at the Hollow Pine Inn, hosted by a music foundation—and signed by a name she hasn't spoken in ten years. She burns it in the kitchen sink, then fishes it out. Beat: the past knocking politely.

chapters.title: Flour, Salt, Memory
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, flashback woven through present-day baking. We learn how she and Elodie met at nineteen in this same inn's kitchen, sharing stolen pastries and half-written songs. Beat: tender ache; establish the songbook as their shared artifact.

chapters.title: What Cyrus Left in Vermont
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: the night Cyrus walked out, choosing culinary school over following Elodie's first tour, telling herself love was a luxury she couldn't afford. Beat: guilt fossilized into discipline.

chapters.title: The Loan Officer Smiles
chapters.summary: Present day. Cyrus's loan extension is denied; she has until February to pay or lose the café. Her business partner Priya urges her to take any gig that pays—including the festival. Beat: cornered pragmatism.

chapters.title: Packing the Good Knives
chapters.summary: Cyrus agrees to cater the festival weekend, telling herself it's strictly business. Priya sees through her instantly and says so. Beat: self-deception cracking under friendly scrutiny.

chapters.title: Road North
chapters.summary: Cyrus drives toward the mountains, radio full of songs she used to harmonize to. A weather alert crackles: a storm front closing roads by nightfall. Beat: dread disguised as anticipation.

chapters.title: Hollow Pine Inn
chapters.summary: Cyrus arrives to find the inn half-renovated and nearly empty of staff. The foundation's director apologizes: most guests canceled ahead of the storm. Then the front door opens. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Elodie
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She recognizes Cyrus across the lobby before Cyrus can pretend otherwise. Ten years of stage poise versus one look at the woman who left. Beat: shock sharpened into armor.

chapters.title: Two Rivals, One Kitchen
chapters.summary: Both women discover they're competing for the same foundation grant—one for Cyrus's café, one for Elodie's struggling music school. Forced civility over prep stations. Beat: prickly, electric tension.

chapters.title: Snowfall
chapters.summary: The storm arrives early. Roads close, cell service dies, and the handful of remaining guests evacuate with the director—leaving Cyrus and Elodie alone in the inn for three days. Beat: trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Dinner for Two, Reluctantly
chapters.summary: Cyrus cooks because someone must; Elodie sets the table because she was raised right. First real conversation in a decade, all surface, both listening underneath. Beat: wary thaw.

chapters.title: The Songbook
chapters.summary: Elodie finds their old songbook in the inn's attic while fetching blankets—half-finished lyrics in two handwritings. She brings it down without asking. Beat: the past made physical.

chapters.title: Page Forty-Seven
chapters.summary: They read the unfinished song they wrote the week before Cyrus left. Elodie admits she's never performed it; Cyrus admits she's never stopped hearing it. Beat: grief surfacing as anger.

chapters.title: Why You Left
chapters.summary: The fight ten years deferred: Cyrus's fear of being someone's afterthought, Elodie's certainty that Cyrus never believed in her music—or in them. Both are more right than wrong. Beat: cathartic rupture.

chapters.title: Morning After the Storm
chapters.summary: Cyrus wakes early, bakes in silence, and finds Elodie already awake watching snow-light. An apology neither planned. Beat: fragile truce, first honest warmth.

chapters.title: Teaching Her the Bridge
chapters.summary: Elodie teaches Cyrus the melody she finished alone; Cyrus corrects a chord change and Elodie laughs for the first time in years. They play badly and completely. Beat: joy relearning its shape.

chapters.title: The Grant
chapters.summary: Sober conversation: only one of them can win the foundation grant. Cyrus realizes winning might mean taking the roof off Elodie's school. Beat: stakes made personal.

chapters.title: Phone Signal Returns
chapters.summary: Service restores; reality floods in—bank calls, festival emails, Elodie's manager demanding she return for a recording session. The bubble pops. Beat: intrusion of the world.

chapters.title: Priya's Voicemail
chapters.summary: Cyrus learns the café's landlord has a cash buyer waiting if she defaults. Back home, everything she built is being priced for sale. Beat: panic and helplessness.

chapters.title: An Offer in the Lobby
chapters.summary: The foundation director returns and offers Cyrus the grant outright—if she relocates to run the inn's kitchen year-round. Everything she needs, somewhere Elodie isn't. Beat: temptation wearing a rescue's face.

chapters.title: Elodie's Confession
chapters.summary: Elodie admits she engineered the invitation—she wanted to see Cyrus again and dressed it up as professional coincidence. Beat: vulnerability as risk; trust shaken and deepened at once.

chapters.title: Anger, Then Honesty
chapters.summary: Cyrus rages at being maneuvered, then stops mid-sentence, realizing she'd have invented a reason to come anyway. They say the true thing at last: neither ever stopped loving the other. Beat: climax of feeling, not yet of plot.

chapters.title: One Night, No Promises
chapters.summary: They spend the last storm-bound evening together without resolving anything—cooking, playing, sleeping in the same room, agreeing not to decide anything until the roads open. Beat: suspended tenderness.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Roads reopen. Packing the car becomes an exercise in not saying goodbye. They exchange numbers like people who mean it this time. Beat: bittersweet parting with a thread attached.

chapters.title: Home to Empty Registers
chapters.summary: Cyrus returns to find the café worse than she left and Priya exhausted from holding it together. The grant offer sits in her inbox like a loaded question. Beat: reality's cold welcome.

chapters.title: The Cash Buyer's Terms
chapters.summary: Cyrus meets the buyer—a chain bakery group offering to keep her on as manager of her own former café. Erasure dressed as salvation. Beat: identity under threat.

chapters.title: First Call
chapters.summary: Elodie calls from tour, voice rough from shows. They talk forty minutes about nothing important and both know it means everything. Beat: long-distance hope, cautious and real.

chapters.title: The Song Goes Public
chapters.summary: A bootleg of Elodie performing 'Page Forty-Seven'—dedicated to 'the one who taught me the bridge'—goes viral. Cyrus hears her own chord change broadcast to strangers. Beat: private history made public; terror and pride entwined.

chapters.title: Everyone Knows Now
chapters.summary: Regulars, Priya, even Cyrus's estranged mother reach out about the song. The invisibility Cyrus curated collapses. Beat: exposure as both wound and liberation.

chapters.title: Deadline Week
chapters.summary: Final notice from the bank. Cyrus must sign with the chain, accept the relocation grant, or lose everything. Elodie texts: 'Whatever you choose, choose you.' Beat: pressure cresting.

chapters.title: What Staying Invisible Cost
chapters.summary: Cyrus walks her empty café at night and understands the truth: safety was just a smaller kind of disappearance. She drafts a counteroffer no one asked for. Beat: epiphany.

chapters.title: The Counteroffer
chapters.summary: Cyrus proposes selling majority stake to a local co-op of her regulars and suppliers—keeping the café alive, herself free. Priya cries; the co-op says yes in principle. Beat: agency reclaimed.

chapters.title: Elodie's Choice
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Offered a headlining solo deal requiring her to drop the school and stop touring small venues, she realizes she's repeating the pattern that broke them. Beat: mirror moment—Elodie must make the choice Cyrus once couldn't.

chapters.title: The Recording Session
chapters.summary: Elodie walks out of the label session mid-take when producers demand she cut 'Page Forty-Seven' entirely. She drives through the night toward Cyrus instead. Beat: sacrifice made visible.

chapters.title: Snow Again
chapters.summary: A late-season storm dusts the coast as Elodie arrives at the café during morning rush, soaked and certain, and asks—not for forgiveness—for a duet. Beat: romantic climax; the grand gesture earned, not manufactured.

chapters.title: Terms of Us
chapters.summary: No fairy tale: they negotiate honestly—tours and seasons, distance and return, the songbook finished jointly. Cyrus chooses the person who sees her, and the work that lets her stay seen. Beat: mature resolution.

chapters.title: Signature Page
chapters.summary: Cyrus signs the co-op papers, keeps a minority share and her recipes, and packs the good knives for the road. Last look at the café that saved her, now saved itself. Beat: release and gratitude.

chapters.title: Encore
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. Six months later: the inn hosts a reopening festival; Elodie and Cyrus perform 'Page Forty-Seven' complete for the first time, Cyrus on harmony and a tray of pastries afterward. Beat: full-circle joy—love inherited, memory sung forward.
